description: ADR-0033 makes chats.publicId a required, client-minted field. Every pre-existing chat row (and every row keyed by a chat) is invalid under the strict schema, so the deployment is wiped rather than migrated: the database is disposable in development and production, and old /c/<convexId> links are intentionally dropped. Each field below is one every row of its table carries, so an expectedCount of 0 states that the table is empty after the wipe. The status stays `migrate` on purpose: the listed fields remain in the schema, and `contracted` would be read by the preflight as a field removal.
cleanupFunction: none: wipe the listed tables with `bunx convex import --table <table> --replace -y --format jsonArray <empty.json>` (an empty `[]` file) on the target deployment before deploying the strict schema; usageLedgerEntries and usageBuckets are user-keyed accounting rows and are left in place (their optional reservationId references dangle by design)
rollback: Redeploy the previous schema (chats without publicId) from origin/main; there is no data to restore because the wipe is intentional.

notes.productionWipeCommand: for t in chats messages generationRuns toolInvocations toolApprovalRequests deletionJobs chatAttachments toolCallLog usageReservations; do bunx convex import --prod --table "$t" --replace -y --format jsonArray empty.json; done
notes.countMethod: bunx convex run --prod --inline-query over each table with take(1001), before and after the wipe
notes.documentContentsPolicy: Only aggregate counts were queried; no production document contents were printed.
